title: Choreography and Motion Mapping
answer: Kinematic generation, notation, motion capture retargeting, crowd simulation and biomechanics.

children.name: Kinematic Video and Generated Movement
children.blurb: Kinematic video and generated movement covers systems that turn recorded or synthetic motion into video, notation, or interactive choreography.

children.name: Dance Notation and Transcription
children.blurb: Dance notation and transcription in AI covers the conversion of human movement into structured, readable symbols or digital records, and the reverse process of turning a score back into motion.

children.name: Motion Capture and Retargeting
children.blurb: Motion capture and retargeting covers recording human movement from sensors or video and mapping that movement onto a different body or character.

children.name: Crowd and Ensemble Simulation
children.blurb: Crowd and ensemble simulation covers the computational generation and coordination of movement for multiple performers or background figures, from large battle scenes and stadium crowds to small dance ensembles.

children.name: Biomechanical Analysis
children.blurb: Biomechanical analysis in choreography and motion mapping uses AI to measure and interpret human movement, from joint angles and muscle activation to balance and force.

sections.body: This field is about using AI to generate, record, and transform human and animal movement. Kinematic video and generated movement use neural networks to create short clips of dancers or figures from text or pose inputs. Dance notation and transcription convert recorded motion into symbolic scores like Labanotation or into simplified stick figures. Motion capture and retargeting take data from sensors or video and map it onto different body shapes or animated characters. Crowd and ensemble simulation coordinates many moving agents so they avoid collisions and follow choreographic rules. Biomechanical analysis measures joint angles, forces, and timing to understand how a body moves.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Generated movement is convincing for a few seconds but often drifts, loses contact with the floor, or produces impossible joint rotations. Dance notation from video is still error prone, especially for fast or occluded movement, and most systems work best on a single dancer in a clean studio. Motion capture retargeting is mature for simple rigs but struggles with loose clothing, props, and close physical contact. Crowd simulation is reliable for background characters in games and film, yet it rarely captures the expressive timing of a real ensemble. Biomechanical analysis is accurate in controlled lab settings but not yet robust enough for everyday video from a phone.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader looking for how AI creates new dance footage should start with Kinematic Video and Generated Movement, which explains the current generation methods and their visual artifacts. Dance Notation and Transcription is the page for anyone who wants to turn existing performance into a readable score or archive. Motion Capture and Retargeting covers the pipeline from sensor data to a usable animated character, including the common failure points. Crowd and Ensemble Simulation is where the focus shifts from one body to many, showing how rules and learned behaviors produce group motion. Biomechanical Analysis connects these artistic tools to measurement, useful for understanding injury risk or technique but not as a substitute for a clinician.
